(b) The pre-spec test with the same removal: [AC:spec-1-1] and [AC:spec-1-2] pass; only [AC:spec-1-3] fails, by chance (on-demand headroom fell to 280 < 600). flows.expected: Caps and other tests unchanged and green; printed counts equal the counts before this spec.

observations.actual: Printed: every-spec 12177 (cap 12256, 79 spare), on-demand 20561 (cap 21163, 602 spare). Diff 1780c88..429d63f on tests/payload-guard.test.ts: two test titles gain a tag and one assertion block is added; no cap, helper or other test changes. git diff 1780c88 HEAD -- payload/ is empty.

findings.summary: Pin vs the real load set: 11 of the 12 paths are named unconditionally per spec by the six skill/agent files or the packet readFirst (dispatch-preflight.mjs:400: testing skill, testing.md, completion.md, dispatch.md, worktrees.md; decompose names workflow.md#commitment-and-queue at :11). But testing-review.md is also named unconditionally: verify SKILL.md:45 and joycraft-reviewer.md:29-30 say to judge each changed test file by #test-changes, joycraft-implementer.md:30 and decompose SKILL.md:31 name it too, and every spec carries a Test changes section. It stays on-demand (the [AC:spec-1-1] test asserts it is on-demand). Moving it would put the every-spec count far over its cap.
findings.assumption: The 1.9.0 split-cap decision classed the test review on-demand, and this spec forbids changing the split rule; the pin matches that decision, not a fresh crawl.

findings.summary: .joycraft/references/gates.md is named by no every-spec skill or agent file, by the packet readFirst, or by gate.mjs; only setup.md:314 and the entry skill (:112) link it. Its every-spec reason ("the gate check and Stop hook run on every spec once gates are on") is runtime behavior, not text an agent reads per spec. The pin keeps it every-spec as the spec says.
findings.assumption: Keeping it every-spec is the stricter (lower-cap) reading and matches the spec.
